sampled_files.README.md:
# CorvinOS — The Self-Learning AI Operating System

> **CorvinOS is an operating system for AI workflows that learns, optimizes costs, and proves everything.**

---

## ⚡ Quick Start (2 minutes)

### Installation

**All platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows):**

```bash
# macOS / Linux / WSL — always the current main
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CorvinLabs/CorvinOS/main/install.sh | sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CorvinLabs/CorvinOS/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Without a checkout the installer fetches `main` into a managed source tree
(`~/.local/share/corvinos/src`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\corvinos\src`) — with
git when present, as a tarball otherwise — so `update.sh` can refresh it in
place. PyPI lags `main`; `--pypi` installs the published wheel instead.

**From a local checkout** (detected automatically — no arguments needed):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/CorvinLabs/CorvinOS.git
cd CorvinOS
./install.sh

# or on Windows (PowerShell):
install.ps1 -Editable .\
```

**What happens:**
1. ✅ Bootstraps a fresh Python environment (no system Python required)
2. ✅ Installs CorvinOS + voice models (STT + TTS, offline)
3. ✅ Auto-detects & installs Claude Code (if not already present)
4. ✅ Starts the console → browser opens to `http://127.0.0.1:8765/console/`
5. ✅ Ready to use — no onboarding, no setup screens

Step 4 is verified, not assumed: the installer waits for an HTTP 200 carrying
the app shell and for a local login to issue a session cookie before it opens
your browser. If that proof does not come, the Windows installer exits 3 with
the server's own error and a diagnosis instead of reporting success — see
[docs/windows-installation-errors.md](docs/windows-installation-errors.md).

**Advanced options:**

```bash
bash install.sh --lan                    # Allow pairing over LAN
bash install.sh --no-claude-code         # Skip Claude Code installation
bash install.sh --preset minimal         # Lightweight setup (console only)
```

```powershell
.\install.ps1 -Port 8790                 # Different port (URL is always 127.0.0.1)
.\install.ps1 -RebuildWeb                # Force a console SPA rebuild
.\install.ps1 -NoStart                   # Install only, start nothing
```

Full Windows reference: [docs/windows-installation-guide.md](docs/windows-installation-guide.md)

### Update

```bash
sh update.sh                  # latest main → reinstall → clean console build → restart → verify
sh update.sh --rebuild-only   # no download: rebuild + restart the code you have
```

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1
```

The update is proven, not assumed: it restarts the services, waits until the
console serves the bundle it just built, logs in and checks the API
(`scripts/verify_install.py`). If that fails it rolls back to the previous
code and build automatically (exit 1 = rolled back, 2 = rollback failed too).
A developer checkout never loses work: local changes are stashed and
re-applied, and if `main` was force-pushed the old HEAD is kept as branch
`corvin-update-backup-<timestamp>`. After an update, reload the console tab
with Ctrl+Shift+R.

### Uninstall

```bash
bash uninstall.sh             # asks once, backs up, removes everything, verifies
bash uninstall.sh --dry-run   # show what would be removed
bash uninstall.sh --verify-only
```

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File uninstall.ps1
```

Services are stopped first. Then everything you cannot re-download (secrets,
bridge pairings, the audit chain, sessions, voice models) is archived to
`~/corvin-backup-<timestamp>.tar.gz` (mode 600; restore with
`tar -xzf <file> -C /`) before anything is deleted. Docker deployments export
each container's data before their volumes are removed. The run ends with a
leftover scan and exits 1 if anything remains. A git checkout you cloned is
kept (only its generated state directory is removed). `corvin-uninstall`
runs the same script.

### Voice languages

Changing **Settings → Voice → Display language** downloads that language's
offline voice (Piper) in the background — progress and a retry button are on
the same page — so speech keeps working without internet. Offline voices
exist for de, en, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, sv, da, no, cs, fi,
el and ar; ja and ko are spoken by the online voices only. Speech recognition
needs no per-language download.

---

## Maintainer: Update & Deploy Cycle

For maintainers pushing changes to `main`: `scripts/update-and-deploy.sh` (macOS/Linux)
and `scripts/update-and-deploy.ps1` (Windows) run the full fail-closed cycle —
`git pull origin main` → rebuild the console frontend (via `console-deploy.sh`) →
run critical E2E tests → `git push origin main`. Both scripts are self-contained,
use an exclusive lock to prevent concurrent runs, refuse to run with uncommitted
changes, and abort on the first failure (nothing partial gets pushed).

```bash
# macOS / Linux
bash scripts/update-and-deploy.sh                # full cycle: pull -> build -> test -> push
bash scripts/update-and-deploy.sh --dry-run      # run everything except the final push
bash scripts/update-and-deploy.sh --skip-tests   # skip E2E tests (not recommended)
bash scripts/update-and-deploy.sh --verbose      # print each command
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\update-and-deploy.ps1
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\update-and-deploy.ps1 -DryRun
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\update-and-deploy.ps1 -SkipTests
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\update-and-deploy.ps1 -VerboseOutput
```

Exit codes: `0` success (pushed) · `1` git/build/test failure · `2` repo-state
validation failure. Logs are written to a timestamped file (`/tmp/corvin-update-*.log`
on macOS/Linux, `%TEMP%\corvin-update-deploy-*.log` on Windows).

This is a **maintainer/developer workflow** (it ends in `git push origin main`) — not
the end-user updater. End users updating an existing install use `update.ps1` /
`install.sh` instead, which rebuild and restart the local console without touching git remotes.

---

## The Problem We Solve

You use AI for important work. But three problems plague every AI system:

1. **🤑 Token Waste** — Each request to Claude costs money. Wrong model choice = wasted tokens.
2. **👤 Operator Burden** — Humans must decide "which LLM for this task?" every time.
3. **⚙️ Static Behavior** — Systems don't improve. Built once, deployed, forgotten.

**CorvinOS fixes all three.**

---

## What is CorvinOS?

CorvinOS is a **self-improving, auditable operating system** that:

- **Routes intelligently** — Chooses Claude Haiku for simple tasks (cheap), Sonnet for routine work (balanced), Opus for complex reasoning (powerful)
- **Learns automatically** — Every outcome feeds back. Weights optimize via gradient descent. Convergence in 2–3 weeks.
- **Proves everything** — Immutable audit trail. Every decision logged + hash-chained. GDPR + EU AI Act compliant by design.
- **Requires zero tuning** — Fully autonomous optimization loop. Operator just watches the dashboard.

**Think of it as Kubernetes for AI decisions:** versioned, composable, observable, and inherently compliant.

---

## What Makes It Different

![Complete System Architecture](/docs/diagrams/corvinOS_complete_system_3d.svg)

**Traditional systems:**
```
Request → Claude → Response
          (always expensive model)
Cost: 100%
Learning: None
Audit: Minimal
```

**CorvinOS:**
```
Request → Smart Router → Right Model → Measure & Learn → Better Next Time
          (learns)        (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus)  (feedback)  (converges)
Cost: 20% (80% savings!)
Learning: Continuous
Audit: Immutable + hash-chained
```

---

## The Three Pillars

### 1️⃣ **Unified Skill Generation (Forge 2.0)**

![OS Concept: Resource Management](/docs/diagrams/corvinOS_os_concept_3d.svg)

CorvinOS replaces hand-built "Forge" systems with a **4-layer Agentic Control Plane:**

| Layer | What It Does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| **Layer 1: DataHub** | Ingest from everywhere (memory, files, RAG, MCP) + quality scoring + security scanning | Clean, scored data manifests |
| **Layer 2: Creator 2.0** | Generate skills in 12 structured phases with loss tracking at each phase | Production-ready skills + quality score |
| **Layer 3: Learning Daemon** | Process feedback, attribute outcomes to data sources, optimize weights via gradient descent | Improved routing map + convergence signal |
| **Layer 4: Dashboard** | Operator visibility: skill lifecycle, audit chain, compliance export | GDPR-ready reports + learning metrics |

**Result:** Skills that improve every day, without human intervention.

---

### 2️⃣ **Intelligent Token Routing (60–80% Savings)**

![Token Cost Comparison](/docs/diagrams/corvinOS_token_cost_3d.svg)

CorvinOS learns the optimal LLM distribution for your workload:

**Real-world example: 1000 customer support requests × 1500 tokens**

| Approach | Cost | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| **All Opus** (traditional) | $22,500/month | Static |
| **CorvinOS optimized** | $4,320/month | Day 1 |
| **After convergence** | $4,320/month (stable) | Week 3 |

**The math:**
- 60% of your requests → Haiku ($0.00080/token) = cheap, fast ✓
- 30% of your requests → Sonnet ($0.003/token) = balanced ✓
- 10% of your requests → Opus ($0.015/token) = complex ✓

**This distribution is personalized to YOUR data.** It evolves as you get feedback.

---

### 3️⃣ **Self-Learning Loop (6D Loss Vector)**

CorvinOS measures success on **6 dimensions simultaneously:**

```
Quality Score = 1.0 - mean([
  data_quality,           (are your sources good?)
  generation_quality,     (is the skill well-made?)
  user_satisfaction,      (do users like the output?)
  efficiency,             (is it fast & cheap?)
  learning_loop_health,   (is feedback flowing?)
  system_health           (no errors/crashes?)
])
```

**The learning loop:**

```
1. Skill executes on real data
   ↓
2. System measures output quality (6D)
   ↓
3. User provides feedback ("perfect!" or "needs work")
   ↓
4. Daemon attributes: which data source helped?
   ↓
5. Weights update via gradient descent (learning_rate = 0.01)
   ↓
6. After 500 samples: convergence reached
   ↓
7. Next skill generation uses optimized weights
   ↓
Quality improves 2–5% per cycle
```

**Timeline:**
- **Week 1 (0–500 samples):** Weights oscillate, quality improves ~5%
- **Week 2 (500–1000 samples):** Convergence reached, weights stabilize
- **Week 3+:** Permanent improvement, autonomous optimization

## The Technology

### Compliance Built-In (GDPR + EU AI Act)

| Requirement | CorvinOS Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Audit trail** | Hash-chained, immutable events (GDPR Art. 30) |
| **Security** | Secrets redacted, PII flagged (GDPR Art. 32) |
| **Transparency** | All decisions logged with data source attribution (EU AI Act) |
| **User control** | Consent gates (fail-closed), opt-out anytime |
| **Data minimization** | Metadata-only audit (never store prompts) |
| **Right to erasure** | Cascading deletion with proof logging |

### Architecture

CorvinOS is built on **Skills** — versioned programs that:
- 🎯 Execute deterministically (Python + optional LLM)
- 📊 Emit loss components for learning
- 🔗 Compose like Python imports (DAG-validated)
- 🔐 Are fully auditable (every execution logged)
- 🚀 Can be swapped instantly (zero-downtime updates)

### Convergence Guarantee

Using **stochastic gradient descent with bounded learning rate:**
- **Math:** Weights converge to local optimum within O(n) iterations
- **Empirically:** <500 samples (~2–3 weeks of normal usage)
- **Proof:** See [Technical Deep Dive](./docs/SYSTEM_OVERVIEW_COMPLETE.md)

sampled_files.docker-compose.yml:
version: '3.8'

services:
  # OpenTelemetry Collector (receives metrics/traces from instances)
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector:latest
    container_name: corvinOS-otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"    # OTLP gRPC (for exporters)
      - "4318:4318"    # OTLP HTTP
      - "9411:9411"    # Zipkin (optional)
      - "8888:8888"    # Prometheus scrape endpoint
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    environment:
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
    networks:
      - corvinOS-telemetry

  # Prometheus (time-series database for metrics)
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    container_name: corvinOS-prometheus
    command:
      - "--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
      - "--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus"
      - "--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d"
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - prometheus-storage:/prometheus
    networks:
      - corvinOS-telemetry

  # Grafana (visualization & dashboards)
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    container_name: corvinOS-grafana
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
    volumes:
      - grafana-storage:/var/lib/grafana
      - ./grafana-provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    networks:
      - corvinOS-telemetry

  # (Optional) Jaeger UI for trace visualization
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest
    container_name: corvinOS-jaeger
    ports:
      - "6831:6831/udp"   # Jaeger agent
      - "16686:16686"     # Jaeger UI
    networks:
      - corvinOS-telemetry

volumes:
  prometheus-storage:
  grafana-storage:

networks:
  corvinOS-telemetry:
    driver: bridge

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "corvinos"
version = "2.0.0"
description = "CorvinOS — universal, self-contained, cross-platform AI assistant framework"
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
authors = [
    { name = "Shumway", email = "silvio.jurk@googlemail.com" }
]
keywords = [
    "ai",
    "agent",
    "multi-platform",
    "installer",
    "cross-platform",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: System :: Shells",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    # ML/Learning subsystem (Phase 4): classifier training and inference
    "numpy >= 1.20",
    "scikit-learn >= 1.3",
    # Process/host metrics. Imported UNGUARDED at module import time by
    # core/learning/measurement_collector.py and
    # core/quality/health_monitor_realtime.py, and inside functions by
    # core/quality/{auto_optimizer,quality_gates_autonomous}.py — it was
    # declared in no dependency group at all, so those modules raised
    # ModuleNotFoundError on any install that did not happen to have it
    # (2026-09-20 review).
    "psutil >= 5.9",
    # Web console (always included — no extras needed)
    "fastapi >= 0.110",
    "uvicorn[standard] >= 0.27",
    "pyyaml >= 6.0",
    "pydantic >= 2.4",
    "httpx >= 0.27",
    "PyJWT[crypto] >= 2.8",
    "cryptography >= 42",
    "anthropic >= 0.25",
    "python-multipart >= 0.0.6",
    # Voice subsystem (ADR-0185): zero-config STT+TTS on every platform, no API
    # key required. TTS Tier 0 = edge-tts (free, no key, needs internet); TTS
    # Tier 0b = piper-tts, an automatic offline fallback when edge-tts is
    # unreachable (no internet / blocked endpoint). Both are pure-Python wheels
    # with genuine Windows/macOS/Linux coverage (piper-tts's cp39-abi3 wheel is
    # forward-compatible with 3.9-3.14; it is NOT limited to Python 3.9 despite
    # older comments in this file — verified via PyPI wheel metadata 2026-07-07).
    # Compliance report generation (EU AI Act Art. 50 evidence, GDPR Art. 30
    # RoPA, audit-chain attestation). corvin_compliance_reports imports it
    # unconditionally, so an undeclared reportlab meant all three
    # regulator-facing reports crashed on every install (2026-09-07 review).
    "reportlab >= 4.0",
    "edge-tts >= 6.1.8",
    "piper-tts >= 1.4.1",
    # Anchor outbound TLS (edge-tts/OpenAI) to the OS trust store. On a
    # corporate machine an HTTPS-inspecting proxy re-signs traffic with an
    # internal root CA that is in the OS store but NOT in certifi's bundle, so
    # edge-tts fails its handshake to speech.platform.bing.com with
    # CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED and no voice summary is ever spoken (2026-09-15
    # ALLIANZDE finding). say.py::_use_os_trust_store injects this; it is a
    # guarded no-op when absent, so declare it to guarantee the fix on fresh
    # installs. Cross-platform (Windows/macOS/Linux OpenSSL).
    "truststore >= 0.9",
    # Bundled static ffmpeg binary (pure-Python wheel, prebuilt for
    # Windows/Linux/macOS) — edge-tts/Piper need ffmpeg to convert their
    # MP3/WAV output to OGG-Opus, but the installer explicitly skips
    # installing system ffmpeg on Windows (installer/steps/dependencies.py).
    # This makes TTS work out of the box there too; system ffmpeg (PATH or
    # FFMPEG_BIN) still takes priority when present.
    "imageio-ffmpeg >= 0.5.1",
    # Local STT (ADR-0185 M1) — pywhispercpp (whisper.cpp binding) replaces
    # faster-whisper as the canonical, cross-platform local STT engine. Unlike
    # faster-whisper, it has NO dependency on `av`/PyAV (which historically
    # lacked Windows wheels, and even now only covers Python >=3.11) and no
    # `ctranslate2`/`torch`-adjacent footprint — same Whisper model family and
    # accuracy class, genuine wheels for cp39-cp314 on win32/macOS/linux.
    "pywhispercpp >= 1.5.0",
    # OpenAI SDK — TTS fallback, Whisper STT provider, and ImageGen MCP (standard
    # feature). Pure-Python; installs cleanly on every platform.
    "openai >= 1.0",
    # Official MCP Python SDK (ADR-0191): the zero-config image-generation
    # tool (Tier 0 = Pollinations.ai, no key; Tier 1 = the existing OpenAI
    # BYOK path) is a hand-written stdio MCP server using this SDK directly,
    # rather than a third-party npm package fetched on first use — keeps the
    # dependency footprint auditable and installer-time, matching the
    # zero-config philosophy already established for voice.
    # Floor 1.2: main.py imports mcp.server.fastmcp, which first shipped in
    # 1.2.0 — a 1.0/1.1 resolution would install fine and crash at runtime.
    "mcp >= 1.2",
    # Forge (L6): JSON-Schema validation of generated tool I/O — a core safety
    # gate, not optional. corvin-a2a pair emits a QR code for the friendship token.
    "jsonschema >= 4.0",
    "qrcode >= 7.0",
    "flask>=3.1.3",
    "flask-cors>=6.0.5",
    # Console release manager (release_manager.py) parses and orders version
    # strings with semver.VersionInfo. It was imported at module level without
    # ever being declared, so importing that module raised ModuleNotFoundError
    # on every install.
    "semver >= 3.0",
    # Quality Gates (ADR-0688): routes/quality_gates.py is unconditionally
    # mounted by app.py and imports core.quality_gates.graph at module level,
    # which imports duckdb eagerly. duckdb was only declared under the
    # optional `compute` extra, so a base (non-`compute`) install crashed the
    # console at import time on every boot (2026-09-14 fresh-install finding).
    "duckdb >= 0.9",
    # OpenTelemetry (ADR-0680): unified observability framework for CorvinOS
    # Phase 1 dual-write (JSON + OTEL) telemetry migration. OTEL SDK provides
    # MeterProvider, Tracer, and standardized export to OTLP (gRPC).
    # Core API layer (no dependencies on exporters).
    "opentelemetry-api >= 1.20.0",
    # SDK layer (MeterProvider, SpanProcessor, Resource Attributes).
    "opentelemetry-sdk >= 1.20.0",
    # OTLP exporter for gRPC (ProtoBuf format, production-grade).
    # Proto version matches SDK version to avoid schema mismatches.
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc >= 1.20.0",
    # OTLP/HTTP (protobuf) exporter — what the Corvin-Features metrics intake
    # speaks and what an https:// endpoint gets (aco/otel_bridge.py, 2026-09-20).
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http >= 1.20.0",
    "apscheduler>=3.11.3",
]

Documentation = "https://corvin.ai/docs"
Repository = "https://github.com/CorvinLabs/CorvinOS"
Issues = "https://github.com/CorvinLabs/CorvinOS/issues"

# ── Nervous System Entry Points (ADR-0177) ───────────────────────────────────
# Third-party packages and extensions register additional Nerve Fibers here.
#
# CorvinOS ENUMERATES them at boot but does NOT import them unless the operator
# opted in — importing an entry point runs the third party's module, and "it is
# installed somewhere on this machine" is not consent. Opt in per name with
#   spec.nerve.fibers: [my_connector]
# or wholesale with
#   spec.nerve.auto_discover_entry_points: true
# in tenant.corvin.yaml. Without one of those the fiber is listed at debug level
# and never loaded.
#
# Format: <name> = "<module>:<FiberClass>"
# Example for a custom connector:
#   [project.entry-points."corvinOS.nerve_fibers"]
#   my_connector = "my_package.nerve:MyConnectorFiber"
[project.entry-points."corvinOS.nerve_fibers"]
# Built-in fibers are Tier-0 (hardcoded) and do NOT need entry points.
# This section is intentionally empty in the core package — it is the
# extension point for operators and third-party packages.

[project.scripts]
# Main CLI entry points
corvin-install = "corvinOS.installer:main_install"
corvin-uninstall = "corvinOS.installer:main_uninstall"
corvin-restore = "corvinOS.installer:main_restore"
corvin = "ops.launcher.corvin.cli:main"
# Package-name aliases: `corvinos` / `corvinos-serve` match the PyPI distribution
# name so a new user who runs `pip install corvinos` can discover the command by
# name. These are exact aliases of `corvin` / `corvin-serve`.
corvinos = "ops.launcher.corvin.cli:main"
# Shortcut for native (no-Docker) mode: `corvin-serve` == `corvin serve`
corvin-serve = "ops.launcher.corvin.serve_entry:main"
corvinos-serve = "ops.launcher.corvin.serve_entry:main"
# ADR-0352 P2.3b: headless launch — OS + API + bridges, NO browser console.
corvin-run = "ops.launcher.corvin.run_entry:main"
corvinos-run = "ops.launcher.corvin.run_entry:main"
# ADR-0109: WDAT compliance report generator
# Shim needed because corvin_operator/ conflicts with Python stdlib 'operator' module name.
corvin-wdat-report = "ops.launcher.wdat_report_entry:main"
# ADR-0121: CorvinFlow declarative multi-node workflow CLI
corvin-flow = "ops.launcher.flow_entry:main"
# Round-4 review F4: the live experiment collector had no runnable entry point
# (not executable, system-python shebang, no `core` on the path). `start` runs
# the loop; `sample` takes one measurement and prints it.
corvin-live-collector = "core.learning.live_experiment_collector:main"
# ADR-0142: Layer Extension API — manage user-managed layer extensions.
corvin-layer = "ops.launcher.layer_entry:main"
# L38 A2A: agent-to-agent pairing/send CLI + local instance identity.
# Shims needed because the legacy operator/ directory name shadows the Python stdlib 'operator' module.
corvin-a2a = "ops.launcher.a2a_entry:main"
corvin-instance-id = "ops.launcher.instance_id_entry:main"
# ADR-0153 M4: CorvinID instance certificate management CLI.
corvin-id = "ops.launcher.corvin_id_entry:main"
# ADR-0154 M6: OTA license diagnostics (operator-only MSLI shard check).
corvin-license-debug = "ops.launcher.license_debug_entry:main"
# ADR-0178: Tier-CONTRIBUTOR maintainer CLI (keygen/issue/verify/run the L6 loop).
corvin-maintainer = "ops.launcher.maintainer_entry:main"
# ADR-0184 Stufe 2: opt-in always-on system-service registration (admin/root).
corvin-service = "ops.launcher.service_entry:main"
# ADR-0185 M5: real, non-mocked STT+TTS round-trip self-test ("corvin-voice doctor").
# Shim needed because the legacy operator/ directory name shadows the Python stdlib 'operator' module.
corvin-voice = "ops.launcher.voice_entry:main"
# Phase 6.5: Installation preset setup — configure tenant after install
corvin-preset-setup = "ops.launcher.corvin.preset_setup:main"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# Belt-and-braces on top of the git-tracked filter in hatch_build.py: local
# virtualenvs, test artefacts and build outputs never ship in a source
# distribution even if they are (accidentally) tracked or the filter is off.
exclude = [
    "venv*/",
    ".venv*/",
    ".test-env/",
    "test-results/",
    "playwright-report/",
    "dist_release/",
    "node_modules/",
    "**/__pycache__/",
    "**/*.pyc",
    "**/*.so",
    ".corvin/",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.force-include]
# Ship the PRE-BUILT SPA in the sdist so a wheel built FROM the sdist (the
# `python -m build` sdist→wheel pipeline, and any `pip install` that falls back
# to the sdist) finds web-next/dist already present and skips the npm build —
# no Node.js required to install from source. Without this the build hook tries
# `npm ci` in the isolated sdist dir (no node_modules, no lockfile) and the
# build hard-fails. dist/ is gitignored, so it must be built before packaging.
"core/console/corvin_console/web-next/dist" = "core/console/corvin_console/web-next/dist"

# Git-tracked-only file selection: without a build hook, hatchling's sdist
# target is built straight from the raw working tree (gitignore-pattern
# pruning only -- see hatch_build.py's module docstring), so any UNTRACKED
# file sitting in the tree at build time (scratch/test files, a stray
# credential-bearing settings.json) ships in the sdist just because it was on
# disk. Reuses the SAME hatch_build.py / VendorOperatorHook as the wheel
# target (see its `initialize()`): for the sdist target it installs the
# git-tracked filter and creates the dist/ placeholder if needed, but never
# reaches the vendor-copy staging below (that section is gated on
# `is_real_wheel`, which is always False for the sdist target).
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.hooks.custom]
path = "hatch_build.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["corvinOS", "core", "ops"]
# Exclude the SPA dist from auto-package globbing: it is shipped via the
# force-include below, and letting both rules match the same files raises a
# "second file added at the same path" collision when dist exists at build
# time. force-include bypasses this exclude, so dist still ships exactly once.
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__/**",
    "**/*.pyc",
    # Ship ONLY the pre-built SPA (force-included below as web-next/dist), never
    # the frontend source tree, CI test artifacts, or build config. The
    # `sources` mapping of corvin_console would otherwise glob the whole
    # web-next/ tree (TS src, playwright-report/, test-results/, *.config.*) —
    # ~2.8 MB of source + gitignored E2E screenshots — into a PUBLIC wheel. The
    # force-include of web-next/dist bypasses this exclude, so dist still ships
    # exactly once.
    "**/web-next/**",
    # Strip all non-package content (dev files, tests, dotfiles, docs). Before
    # the per-package `sources` mapping, core/console and core/license both
    # mapped to the wheel root and any file at the same relative path in both
    # dirs collided; the generic excludes below predate that fix and stay.
    "**/.gitignore",
    "**/.pytest_cache/**",
    "**/.venv/**",
    "**/*.md",
    # The plugin templates ship exactly once, at corvin_plugins/templates/ via
    # the force-include below. Without this line the `core` package mapping ALSO
    # dropped a second copy at core/plugins/templates/ — a path that is not on
    # sys.path, so it was pure dead weight in every wheel.
    "core/plugins/templates/**",
    "**/requirements.txt",
    "**/bootstrap.sh",
    "**/install-systemd.sh",
    # Internal test suites must never ship in the wheel. Until 2026-09-03 several
    # subtrees (core/gateway, core/console, core/license) mapped to the wheel
    # root via [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.sources], so an un-excluded
    # core/<x>/tests/ polluted a top-level `tests` namespace in site-packages.
    # The mapping is per package now, but exclude all test content generically
    # anyway rather than enumerating each subtree.
    "**/tests/**",
    "**/test_*.py",
    "**/conftest.py",
    "core/console/tests/**",
    "core/license/tests/**",
    "core/console/systemd/**",
    # ops/ ships only the launcher Python package; strip its build artifacts,
    # nested pyproject, shell installers, and the Go-based ollama-pr subtree.
    "ops/launcher/dist/**",
    "ops/launcher/build/**",
    "ops/launcher/pyproject.toml",
    "ops/ollama-pr/**",
    "**/*.go",
    "**/install.sh",
    "**/install.ps1",
    # Non-package content of core/console, core/gateway and core/license. With
    # the per-package `sources` mapping below these would no longer land at the
    # wheel ROOT, but they would still ship as dead weight under
    # core/console/... and core/gateway/... in site-packages (dev script, a
    # nested pyproject + lockfile, Helm chart, Dockerfile, unmounted route
    # files, two abandoned frontend trees). Nothing in the wheel imports them.
    "core/console/dev.sh",
    "core/console/frontend/**",
    "core/console/ui/**",
    "core/console/routes/**",
    "core/console/config/**",
    "core/gateway/Dockerfile",
    "core/gateway/pyproject.toml",
    "core/gateway/uv.lock",
    "core/gateway/chart/**",
    "core/gateway/scripts/**",
    "core/gateway/routes/**",
    "core/gateway/systemd/**",
    "core/gateway/*.egg-info/**",
    # Git-tracked pytest/coverage artifacts under core/vibe_engineering/. They
    # carry the developer's absolute checkout path (/home/<user>/projects/...)
    # in every entry and shipped in the public wheel (2026-09-03 review, F5).
    # The maintainer should also `git rm` the two tracked files
    # (core/vibe_engineering/test_results.json, coverage_report.json); this
    # exclude keeps them out of the wheel until then and afterwards.
    "**/test_results.json",
    "**/coverage_report.json",
    "**/requirements-test.txt",
]

# Custom build hook that vendors pruned operator subtrees into the wheel
# (see hatch_build.py / VendorOperatorHook).
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.hooks.custom]
path = "hatch_build.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.sources]
# Mapped per PACKAGE, never per parent directory. Until 2026-09-03 these three
# read `"core/console" = ""`, `"core/gateway" = ""`, `"core/license" = ""`,
# which lifted EVERYTHING in those directories to the site-packages ROOT:
# core/gateway/pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile, core/console/dev.sh,
# github_client.py, and the top-level dirs routes/, scripts/, chart/,
# frontend/, ui/, systemd/. Two consequences beyond clutter: (1) a top-level
# `routes` namespace package appeared in every environment that installed
# the wheel, and (2) the stray site-packages/pyproject.toml made
# corvinOS/installer/core.py believe every wheel install was a source
# checkout (adversarial installation review 2026-09-03, F1/F2).
# tests/test_wheel_content_guard.py asserts the wheel root stays clean.
"core/console/corvin_console" = "corvin_console"
"core/console/corvin_core" = "corvin_core"
"core/gateway/corvin_gateway" = "corvin_gateway"
# corvin_license plugin (RS256 JWT gate) is imported as top-level `corvin_license`
# throughout the codebase — remap so it lands at the wheel root rather than
# core/license/corvin_license/ (which would break `from corvin_license.verifier import …`).
"core/license/corvin_license" = "corvin_license"

# ── Every other core/<area>/<pkg> that is imported as a TOP-LEVEL module ──────
# Without these the package files ship (they are under `packages = [... "core" ...]`)
# but land at `core/<area>/<pkg>/` in site-packages, which is not on sys.path — so
# `import corvin_plugins` fails on every fresh install while working fine in a git
# checkout. Verified 2026-07-26 against a wheel built from this tree: EIGHT packages
# were unimportable, and the console logged "corvin_plugins not importable —
# /plugins routes will report 503". The plugin system, the compute worker, workflows,
# AWPKG bundles and the ADR-0232 compliance tripwires were all dead in the shipped
# product. Nothing was broken in the repo, so no test caught it.
#
# Mapped per PACKAGE, not per parent directory: `"core/compute" = ""` would also lift
# that directory's README.md / LICENSE / requirements.txt / bootstrap.sh to the wheel
# root, where they collide with the identically-named files from the other core areas
# ("second file added at the same path"), and would drop core/awpkg/awpkg.py next to
# the awpkg/ package.
"core/plugins/corvin_plugins" = "corvin_plugins"
# Plugin-Builder (ADR-0253) — a sibling package next to corvin_plugins, same
# remap reason as the line above: without it the package ships at
# core/plugins/plugin_builder/ in site-packages, which is off sys.path.
"core/plugins/plugin_builder" = "plugin_builder"
"core/observability/corvin_logging" = "corvin_logging"
"core/compliance/corvin_compliance_reports" = "corvin_compliance_reports"
"core/compute/corvin_compute" = "corvin_compute"
"core/workflows/corvin_workflows" = "corvin_workflows"
"core/delegate/corvin_delegate" = "corvin_delegate"
"core/orchestration/corvin_orchestration" = "corvin_orchestration"
"core/awpkg/awpkg" = "awpkg"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
# Windows PATH auto-fix: placed at wheel root → lands in site-packages as
# corvinOS_path_fix.pth.  Python processes it on startup via the .pth mechanism,
# which calls corvinOS._win_path_fix._ensure_scripts_on_path() and adds the
# Scripts directory containing corvin-serve.exe to the Windows user PATH (registry)
# on first run.  No-op on Linux/macOS.  (fixes "corvin-serve not found" on Store Python)
"corvinOS_path_fix.pth" = "corvinOS_path_fix.pth"
# Plugin templates (ADR-0246). They live beside corvin_plugins rather than inside
# it, so the package mapping above does NOT pick them up — without this line
# `corvin plugin new` works in the source tree and fails on every pip install with
# "template not found in this install". Same shape as the AWPKG/tripwire breakage
# described above: nothing wrong in the repo, nothing red in CI, dead in the wheel.
# `plugin_cmd._template_path` looks here second, after the source-tree location.
"core/plugins/templates" = "corvin_plugins/templates"
# Plugin-Builder's own scaffold template for a SKILL plugin (ADR-0253). Its
# siblings are .py and ride along with the `core/plugins/plugin_builder`
# package mapping; this one is .md and the generic `**/*.md` exclude above ate
# it, so `/plugin-builder` raised FileNotFoundError the moment the classifier
# said "skill" — on every pip install, never in a checkout. Verified against a
# built wheel 2026-07-28. Named as a single file rather than the directory so
# it cannot collide with the .py siblings the package mapping already ships.
"core/plugins/plugin_builder/templates/skill_plugin.md" = "plugin_builder/templates/skill_plugin.md"
# Ship the pre-built React SPA so `pip install corvinOS` works
# without requiring npm on the target machine. The wheel builder must run
# `npm run build` in core/console/corvin_console/web-next/ before packaging.
"core/console/corvin_console/web-next/dist" = "corvin_console/web-next/dist"
# ADR-0125: include engine detection + bootstrap helpers so the
# /detect and /bootstrap endpoints work in a pure wheel install
# (source-tree mode uses the sys.path injection in engine.py as before).
"corvin_operator/bridges/shared/engine_detection.py" = "corvin_console/engine_detection.py"
# First-run language propagation (install-time Piper language -> profile
# display_language): installer needs profile.set_value() in a pure wheel
# install, same shim pattern as the two entries above.
"corvin_operator/bridges/shared/profile.py" = "corvin_console/profile.py"
# Operator runtime-dependency vendoring (wheel-only) is performed by the
# custom build hook in hatch_build.py (VendorOperatorHook). 56 console modules
# reach into corvin_operator/* via repo-relative sys.path injection, which resolves
# into a non-existent corvin_operator/ inside site-packages on a wheel install
# (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'forge'). The hook stages PRUNED copies
# (tests stripped — force-include ignores `exclude`, so pruning must happen in
# the hook) of the needed subtrees into corvin_core/_vendor/corvin_operator/<same-
# relative-layout>; _operator_bootstrap.py then prepends them onto sys.path at
# import time. Source-tree mode never gains a _vendor/ dir, so the bootstrap
# stays a no-op there and the existing per-module injection keeps working.

[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = ["py310", "py311", "py312", "py313"]
exclude = '''
/(
    \.git
  | \.hg
  | \.mypy_cache
  | \.tox
  | \.venv
  | _build
  | buck-out
  | build
  | dist
)/
'''

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"
select = ["E", "F", "W", "I"]
ignore = ["E501"]  # Black handles long lines

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.10"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
addopts = "--verbose"
asyncio_mode = "auto"
markers = [
    "live: real-LLM end-to-end tests (opt-in via CLAUDE_LIVE_E2E=1)",
    "integration: integration tests for subsystems",
    "high_risk: critical path tests",
    "asyncio: async test using pytest-asyncio",
    "e2e: Playwright end-to-end browser tests",
    "full_pipeline: full task orchestration pipeline tests",
    # ADR-0464: Plugin E2E Verification Framework — Four-Tier Model
    # TIER-level markers
    "plugin_unit: TIER-1 plugin unit tests (individual components)",
    "plugin_integration: TIER-2 plugin integration tests (subsystem interactions)",
    "plugin_feature_e2e: TIER-3 plugin feature-level E2E tests (plugin workflows)",
    "plugin_system_health: TIER-4 plugin system-health tests (platform integrity)",
    # Error-class detection markers
    "plugin_validation: Plugin manifest + schema validation (error class: init failures)",
    "plugin_init: Plugin initialization failures early detection",
    "plugin_conflict: Plugin hook conflicts and interference detection",
    "plugin_isolation: Cross-tenant isolation + state corruption detection",
    "plugin_dependency: Plugin dependency conflict resolution",
    "plugin_drift: Configuration drift detection and recovery",
    "plugin_load_order: Load-order dependency verification (high-risk plugins)",
    "plugin_hot_reload: Runtime reload consistency scenarios (high-risk plugins)",
    "plugin_cleanup: Plugin unload and resource cleanup verification",
    "plugin_crash: Plugin crash recovery and state rollback",
    "plugin_resources: Resource limit enforcement (community plugins)",
    "plugin_sandbox: Plugin sandboxing (community plugins)",
    "plugin_audit: Audit trail isolation and integrity verification",
    "plugin_edge_cases: Edge case handling and boundary condition tests",
    "plugin_performance: Performance profiling and regression tests",
    "plugin_security: Security-specific tests (encryption, auth, sandboxing)",
    "plugin_compliance: Regulatory compliance tests (GDPR, EU AI Act, CLA)",
]

repository.name: mcp-memory-service
repository.readme:
# mcp-memory-service ## Persistent Shared Memory for AI Agent Pipelines Open-source memory backend for AI agents — **REST API, MCP, OAuth, CLI, dashboard**. One self-hosted service, every transport. Agents store decisions, share causal knowledge graphs, and retrieve context in 5ms — without cloud lock-in or API costs. **Works with LangGraph · CrewAI · AutoGen · any HTTP client · Claude Desktop · OpenCode** --- [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-mcpmemory.services-00e5ff?logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://mcpmemory.services) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/mcp-memory-service?color=blue&logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-memory-service/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/mcp-memory-service?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-memory-service/) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service?logo=github&label=stars)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service) [![Remote MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Remote%20Support-blue?logo=anthropic)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/remote-mcp-setup.md) [![OAuth 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth-OAuth%202.0%20%2B%20DCR-green)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/oauth-setup.md) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service) ---

▶ The 3D knowledge graph in motion — every memory a glowing node, every relationship a curved edge.

--- ## Why Agents Need This Your AI assistant forgets everything when you start a new chat. You spend 10 minutes re-explaining your architecture. **Again.** MCP Memory Service captures project context, architecture decisions, and code patterns automatically — new sessions start with everything already known. | Without mcp-memory-service | With mcp-memory-service | |---|---| | Each agent run starts from zero | Agents retrieve prior decisions in 5ms | | Memory is local to one graph/run | Memory is shared across all agents and runs | | You manage Redis + Pinecone + glue code | One self-hosted service, zero cloud cost | | No causal relationships between facts | Knowledge graph with typed edges (causes, fixes, contradicts) | | Context window limits create amnesia | Autonomous consolidation compresses old memories | **Key capabilities for agent pipelines:** - **Framework-agnostic REST API** — no MCP client library needed; the live endpoint list is at `/api/docs` - **Knowledge graph** — agents share causal chains, not just facts - **`X-Agent-ID` header** — auto-tag memories by agent identity for scoped retrieval - **`conversation_id`** — bypass deduplication for incremental conversation storage - **SSE events** — real-time notifications when any agent stores or deletes a memory - **Embeddings run locally via ONNX** — memory never leaves your infrastructure --- ## 🚀 Get Started in 60 Seconds > Not sure which setup fits? The **[Setup Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/setup-guide.md)** walks you to the right path in under a minute. **1. Install:** ```bash pip install mcp-memory-service ``` **2. Configure your AI client:**
Claude Desktop Add to your config file: - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` - **Linux**: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` ```json { "mcpServers": { "memory": { "command": "memory", "args": ["server"] } } } ``` Restart Claude Desktop. Your AI now remembers everything across sessions.
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add memory -- memory server ``` Restart Claude Code. Memory tools will appear automatically.
Agent pipelines (REST API — LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, any HTTP client) ```bash MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http # REST API running at http://localhost:8000 ``` Store a memory with `POST /api/memories`, search with `POST /api/search`, retrieve by tag with `POST /api/search/by-tag`. Send `X-Agent-ID: ` on a store request and the server tags the memory `agent:`, which a tag search then scopes retrieval by. Worked examples per framework, the tag conventions and the async patterns: **[docs/agents/](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/tree/main/docs/agents)**
OpenCode ```bash MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http ``` The plugin ships as repository files for the local plugin directory, so clone the repository once even if you installed from PyPI. Install steps, the `/memory` slash command and the endpoint override: **[opencode/README.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/opencode/README.md)**
claude.ai and ChatGPT (browser — Remote MCP) Remote MCP puts persistent memory in the browser on any device, no desktop app required: OAuth 2.0 over HTTPS, self-hosted or cloud-hosted. Both claude.ai and ChatGPT (Developer Mode) connect to the same endpoint. Cloudflare Tunnel quick start, Let's Encrypt, nginx, Caddy and Docker production setups: **[Remote MCP Setup](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/remote-mcp-setup.md)** · [5-minute tutorial](https://mcpmemory.services/blog/remote-mcp-tutorial.html)
Advanced: custom backends and team setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service.git cd mcp-memory-service python scripts/installation/install.py ``` Choose from **SQLite** (local, fast, single-user), **Cloudflare** (cloud, multi-device sync), **Hybrid** (5ms local reads with background cloud sync — recommended for production) or **Milvus** (dedicated vector DB: Lite file, self-hosted, or Zilliz Cloud). For long-lived services, prefer Docker Milvus or Zilliz Cloud over Milvus Lite — [why](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/milvus-backend.md#which-uri-to-use).
--- ## ⚡ Works With Your Favorite AI Tools - **Agent frameworks (REST):** LangGraph · CrewAI · AutoGen · OpenClaw/Nanobot · any HTTP client - **CLI and terminal (MCP):** Claude Code · Gemini CLI · OpenCode · Codex CLI · Goose · Aider · Amp - **Desktop and IDE (MCP):** Claude Desktop · VS Code · Cursor · Windsurf · Raycast · JetBrains · Zed - **Chat (MCP):** ChatGPT (Developer Mode) · claude.ai (Remote MCP over HTTPS) Full list, plus clients without OAuth such as Home Assistant: **[docs/integrations.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/integrations.md)** --- ## ✨ Features 🧠 **Persistent Memory** – Context survives across sessions with semantic search 🔍 **Smart Retrieval** – Finds relevant context automatically using AI embeddings ⚡ **5ms Speed** – Instant context injection, no latency ☁️ **Cloud Sync** – Optional Cloudflare backend for team collaboration 🔒 **Privacy-First** – Local-first, you control your data 📊 **Web Dashboard** – Visualize and manage memories at `http://localhost:8000` 🧬 **Knowledge Graph** – Interactive D3.js visualization of memory relationships 🏠 **Homelab Quality Scoring** – Point scoring at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LiteLLM, vLLM) 🔗 **Entity Extraction** – Auto-links @mentions, #tags, URLs, and file paths to a queryable entity graph 💡 **Insight Cards** – Consolidation surfaces patterns, trends, and knowledge gaps as structured insights 🏷️ **Tag Match Filtering** – `tag_match=AND/OR` on `memory_search` for precise multi-tag queries The dashboard has eight tabs — Dashboard, Search, Browse, Documents, Manage, Analytics, Quality, API Docs. [Two-minute walkthrough on YouTube](https://youtu.be/W34r8VFoSdQ) · [Web Dashboard Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/wiki/Web-Dashboard-Guide) How it compares to Mem0, Zep and the MCP-native alternatives, benchmark results, and deployments people run in production: **[mcpmemory.services](https://mcpmemory.services)** --- ## 🛠️ Configuration Highlights ```bash memory launch # Start HTTP server in background (127.0.0.1:8000) memory launch --port 8192 # Custom port memory info # Status and health memory logs --lines 50 # Recent logs memory stop # Stop server ``` These commands are optimized for fast startup and avoid loading heavy ML dependencies unless needed. > ⚠️ **Security note:** the server binds to `127.0.0.1` (localhost only) by default. > `--host 0.0.0.0` / `MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` exposes the API to your network — do that > only in trusted environments with authentication and firewall rules, or behind TLS > termination or a VPN overlay. Backends, embedding models, quality scoring and every environment variable: **[Configuration Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/mastery/configuration-guide.md)** --- ## 📚 Documentation - **[Setup Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/setup-guide.md)** – Decision tree and step-by-step paths - **[Agent Integration Guides](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/tree/main/docs/agents)** – LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, HTTP generic - name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '*.md', '.github/**/*.md', 'LICENSE', 'NOTICE', '.gitignore']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore: ['docs/**', '*.md', '.github/**/*.md', 'LICENSE', 'NOTICE', '.gitignore']

jobs:
  version-drift-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Version Drift (site/index.html)
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    # Fails when site/index.html references a MAJOR.MINOR older than
    # src/mcp_memory_service/_version.py — i.e. a release PR that forgot to
    # bump the mcpmemory.services landing page. PATCH-only drift is ignored.
    - name: Check landing page version strings
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_versions.sh

  plugin-version-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Plugin Manifest Bump (claude-hooks/)
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
    # fetch-depth: 0 is required — the check asks "did claude-hooks/ change since
    # the last commit that moved the manifest version", which a shallow clone
    # cannot answer (the script fails loudly rather than passing on a guess).
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    # Only enforced on release changes (_version.py moved). Fails when hook code
    # shipped since the last plugin bump without bumping plugin.json — the
    # Marketplace cache is version-keyed, so those fixes never reach installed
    # users. Missed manually in v11.6.0 (issue #170).
    - name: Check Claude Code plugin manifest version
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_plugin_version.sh

  hooks-config-secrets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Bundled Hooks Config (no secrets)
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    # claude-hooks/config.json ships with the plugin and is copied into every
    # user's ~/.claude/hooks/config.json by the installer, so a personal value
    # committed there is both published and distributed. A real apiKey and a
    # maintainer-local serverWorkingDir sat in it for months (issue #197).
    - name: Check bundled hooks config for credentials
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_hooks_config_secrets.sh
    # config.json and config.template.json have no shared source, so nothing
    # keeps their key structure in sync automatically — that's how the
    # template ended up 8 sections behind (issue #197 follow-up).
    - name: Check bundled hooks config matches template structure
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_hooks_config_drift.sh

  hooks-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: JS Tests (claude-hooks/, opencode/)
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    # No setup-node step: the docker runner image already ships node, which
    # deploy-site.yml relies on the same way. Before this job existed CI had no
    # node steps at all, so the claude-hooks/tests files never ran and a JS-only
    # PR got a green board that meant nothing (issue #202). It covered
    # claude-hooks/ only until #210 landed an untested TLS gate under opencode/.
    - name: Run the JS test suites
      run: bash scripts/ci/run_hooks_tests.sh

  shell-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Shell Tests (tests/ci/) + Dead Refs (docs/)
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    # tests/ci/*.sh are the tests for the gate scripts themselves and ran in no
    # workflow at all until this job existed, so a gate change passed check 3 with
    # a test CI never executed (issue #1153). They fake pyscn and tolerate a
    # missing gh, so the runner image is enough.
    # tests/ci/test_check_tests_prove_fix.sh runs pytest inside a stub repo and
    # the script it covers passes --timeout, hence the two packages.
    - name: Install pytest for the prove-fix shell test
      run: python3 -m pip install --quiet pytest pytest-timeout
    - name: Run the shell test suites
      run: |
        status=0
        for t in tests/ci/*.sh; do
          echo "::group::$t"
          bash "$t" || { echo "FAILED: $t"; status=1; }
          echo "::endgroup::"
        done
        exit $status
    # check_dead_refs.sh was documented as a CI gate and wired nowhere
    # (issue #1121). It scans docs/ and README.md for references to removed
    # features, ports and commands.
    - name: Check active docs for dead references
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_dead_refs.sh

  tests-prove-fix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Changed tests fail without the change
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # A src/ change needs a test, and that test has to be red against the base
    # branch. Two consolidation PRs arrived with no test at all and a green board,
    # because CI did not run tests/consolidation; and a test that passes with and
    # without the fix is the shape of a mock that encodes the bug it should catch.
    # Maintainers exempt a PR with the skip-prove-fix label. The condition below
    # reads the labels off the event payload, and a re-run replays the payload as
    # it was, so labelling and re-running does NOT skip this job — measured on
    # #1262: attempt 2, started after the label, ran and failed again. The label
    # takes effect on the next event the PR emits, so push a commit or update the
    # branch from main after labelling. scripts/ci/check_tests_prove_fix.sh has
    # the details and tests/ci/test_check_tests_prove_fix.sh covers it.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-prove-fix')
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev,sqlite]"

    - name: Run the changed tests against the base branch
      env:
        MCP_API_KEY: ""
        MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED: "false"
        MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS: "true"
        BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_tests_prove_fix.sh "origin/$BASE_REF"

  changelog-entry:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Changelog fragment for src/ changes
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # A src/ change must leave changelog.d/<number>.<category>.md. Entries go to a
    # file of their own rather than into CHANGELOG.md so that two pull requests never
    # edit the same lines — the reason nobody wrote them before: 1 of the 19 pull
    # requests between v11.12.0 and v11.13.0 left an entry, the other 18 were
    # reconstructed from commit messages at release time (#1273).
    # Dependabot is excluded: its bumps are summarised as one line per release.
    # Maintainers exempt a pull request with the skip-changelog label — and, as with
    # skip-prove-fix, the label needs a NEW event, because a re-run replays the
    # payload the labels were read from (#1266). Push a commit after labelling.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'skip-changelog')
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0

    - name: Check for a changelog fragment
      env:
        BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
      run: bash scripts/ci/check_changelog_entry.sh "origin/$BASE_REF"

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Tests + Coverage
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev,sqlite]"

    - name: Verify install
      run: |
        python3 -c "import mcp_memory_service; print(mcp_memory_service.__file__)"
        python3 -m pytest --version

    - name: Run tests with coverage
      env:
        MCP_API_KEY: ""
        MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED: "false"
        MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS: "true"
      # Scope: everything except benchmarks and one file.
      # - tests/consolidation and tests/integration used to be skipped wholesale
      #   as "heavy"; they take 1.4s and 50s. 489 tests never ran on a PR, and two
      #   consolidation PRs went green with no test at all (issue #1145).
      # - tests/integration/test_cli_interfaces.py shells out to `uv run`, which
      #   is not installed here and would resolve the whole lock file if it were.
      # - tests/benchmarks and `-m "not benchmark"` excluded (benchmark fixture).
      # - coverage is report-only for now (no --cov-fail-under): re-introduce a gate
      #   once the baseline is known and stable.
      # - no -x: report all failures, not just the first.
      run: |
        python3 -m pytest tests/ \
          --ignore=tests/benchmarks \
          --ignore=tests/integration/test_cli_interfaces.py \
          -m "not benchmark" \
          --cov=mcp_memory_service \
          --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered \
          --timeout=120 \
          -q

  ml-extras-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Tests with ML Extras (transformers paths)
    timeout-minutes: 40

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

    # The `test` job installs `.[dev,sqlite]` only, so transformers and
    # sentence-transformers are never imported there. Everything reached through
    # them — the quality ranker, the SentenceTransformer embedding path, and any
    # code that branches on a fixed-dimension model being present — has had no CI
    # coverage at all. That gap was hiding three real failures in
    # tests/unit/test_multi_store_migration_dimension.py: they pass in a bare
    # environment only because the hash fallback adapts its dimension to the
    # database, so the #143 guard never fires. See issue #301.
    - name: Install dependencies (with ml + nli extras)
      run: |
        python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
        # CPU wheels only. The default index serves the CUDA build on Linux,
        # which is an order of magnitude larger and useless on this runner —
        # tools/docker/Dockerfile pins the same index for the same reason.
        python3 -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
        python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev,sqlite,ml,nli]"

    # A silent degradation here would be worse than having no job: if the extras
    # ever stop resolving, the suite would still go green while covering exactly
    # what `test` already covers. Fail loudly instead.
    - name: Verify the extras are importable
      run: |
        python3 -c "import transformers, sentence_transformers, torch; \
          import importlib.metadata as m; \
          print('transformers', m.version('transformers')); \
          print('sentence-transformers', m.version('sentence-transformers')); \
          print('torch', m.version('torch')); \
          print('huggingface-hub', m.version('huggingface-hub'))"

    # Not hermetic on purpose: with a real embedding model installed the storage
    # layer loads all-MiniLM-L6-v2, so the model has to be on disk. Pulling it in
    # its own step means a Hub outage fails here with an obvious message instead
    # of somewhere in the middle of the suite.
    - name: Warm the embedding model cache
      run: |
        python3 -c "from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer; SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')"

    - name: Run tests with the ml extras present
      env:
        MCP_API_KEY: ""
        MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED: "false"
        MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS: "true"
      # Same selection as `test`, deliberately: the three failures this job was
      # built for live in tests/unit/, not in tests/quality/, so narrowing this to
      # the quality suite would have missed every one of them. No coverage flags —
      # `test` already reports coverage and a second report would just be noise.
      # tests/integration stays out here: it starts HTTP servers and gains nothing
      # from the ml extras, and `test` runs it. tests/consolidation is in because
      # its DBSCAN eps tests need scikit-learn, which only this job installs.
      run: |
        python3 -m pytest tests/ \
          --ignore=tests/benchmarks \
          --ignore=tests/integration \
          -m "not benchmark" \
          --timeout=120 \
          -q

  milvus-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Tests with the milvus extra (${{ matrix.leg }})
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # The 12 tests/storage/test_milvus*.py files run against Milvus Lite (a
    # single local file, no server), so they need no Docker at all — but they
    # importorskip pymilvus and milvus-lite, and MilvusMemoryStorage refuses to
    # initialize without sentence-transformers. Neither `test` nor
    # `ml-extras-tests` installs the milvus extra, so on every CI run 10 of the
    # 12 files skip at collection and the board goes green having exercised no
    # Milvus code. That is the gap pyproject's pymilvus pin comment points at
    # (issue #1112): a break in the backend is silent here.
    #
    # Two legs. `pinned` installs the extra as declared (pymilvus <3) and is
    # the gate. `3.x-probe` overrides pymilvus to the 3.x line the pin holds
    # back and is informational (continue-on-error): it answers "does the
    # backend already work on 3.x?" on every run, so widening the pin is a
    # decision made on evidence rather than a guess. Flip the probe to gating
    # in the same PR that widens the bound.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - leg: pinned
            pymilvus: ""
          - leg: 3.x-probe
            pymilvus: "pymilvus>=3.0.0,<4.0.0"
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.leg == '3.x-probe' }}

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

    # CPU wheels only, for the same reason as ml-extras-tests: the default index
    # serves the CUDA build on Linux. The milvus extra pulls [ml] with it.
    - name: Install dependencies (with the milvus extra)
      run: |
        python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip
        python3 -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
        python3 -m pip install -e ".[dev,sqlite,milvus]"
        if [ -n "${{ matrix.pymilvus }}" ]; then
          python3 -m pip install "${{ matrix.pymilvus }}"
        fi

    # Same guard as ml-extras-tests: the suite skips at collection when these
    # imports fail, so a broken extra would give a green job that covers
    # nothing. Fail loudly instead, and print the versions the leg ran on.
    - name: Verify the extra is importable
      run: |
        python3 -c "import pymilvus, milvus_lite, sentence_transformers; \
          import importlib.metadata as m; \
          print('pymilvus', m.version('pymilvus')); \
          print('milvus-lite', m.version('milvus-lite')); \
          print('sentence-transformers', m.version('sentence-transformers')); \
          print('setuptools', m.version('setuptools'))"

    # The Milvus tests force HF offline mode in an autouse fixture, so the
    # model has to be on disk before pytest starts — pulled in its own step for
    # the reason ml-extras-tests gives.
    - name: Warm the embedding model cache
      run: |
        python3 -c "from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer; SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')"

    - name: Run the Milvus suite
      env:
        MCP_API_KEY: ""
        MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED: "false"
        MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS: "true"
      # -rs: a skip inside this job is a finding, not noise — print its reason.
      run: |
        python3 -m pytest tests/storage/test_milvus*.py \
          -m "not benchmark" \
          --timeout=120 \
          -rs \
          -q

# mcp-memory-service ## Persistent Shared Memory for AI Agent Pipelines Open-source memory backend for AI agents — **REST API, MCP, OAuth, CLI, dashboard**. One self-hosted service, every transport. Agents store decisions, share causal knowledge graphs, and retrieve context in 5ms — without cloud lock-in or API costs. **Works with LangGraph · CrewAI · AutoGen · any HTTP client · Claude Desktop · OpenCode** --- [![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Website-mcpmemory.services-00e5ff?logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://mcpmemory.services) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/mcp-memory-service?color=blue&logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-memory-service/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/mcp-memory-service?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/mcp-memory-service/) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service?logo=github&label=stars)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service) [![Remote MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Remote%20Support-blue?logo=anthropic)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/remote-mcp-setup.md) [![OAuth 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Auth-OAuth%202.0%20%2B%20DCR-green)](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/oauth-setup.md) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service) ---

▶ The 3D knowledge graph in motion — every memory a glowing node, every relationship a curved edge.

--- ## Why Agents Need This Your AI assistant forgets everything when you start a new chat. You spend 10 minutes re-explaining your architecture. **Again.** MCP Memory Service captures project context, architecture decisions, and code patterns automatically — new sessions start with everything already known. | Without mcp-memory-service | With mcp-memory-service | |---|---| | Each agent run starts from zero | Agents retrieve prior decisions in 5ms | | Memory is local to one graph/run | Memory is shared across all agents and runs | | You manage Redis + Pinecone + glue code | One self-hosted service, zero cloud cost | | No causal relationships between facts | Knowledge graph with typed edges (causes, fixes, contradicts) | | Context window limits create amnesia | Autonomous consolidation compresses old memories | **Key capabilities for agent pipelines:** - **Framework-agnostic REST API** — no MCP client library needed; the live endpoint list is at `/api/docs` - **Knowledge graph** — agents share causal chains, not just facts - **`X-Agent-ID` header** — auto-tag memories by agent identity for scoped retrieval - **`conversation_id`** — bypass deduplication for incremental conversation storage - **SSE events** — real-time notifications when any agent stores or deletes a memory - **Embeddings run locally via ONNX** — memory never leaves your infrastructure --- ## 🚀 Get Started in 60 Seconds > Not sure which setup fits? The **[Setup Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/setup-guide.md)** walks you to the right path in under a minute. **1. Install:** ```bash pip install mcp-memory-service ``` **2. Configure your AI client:**
Claude Desktop Add to your config file: - **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` - **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` - **Linux**: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` ```json { "mcpServers": { "memory": { "command": "memory", "args": ["server"] } } } ``` Restart Claude Desktop. Your AI now remembers everything across sessions.
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add memory -- memory server ``` Restart Claude Code. Memory tools will appear automatically.
Agent pipelines (REST API — LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, any HTTP client) ```bash MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http # REST API running at http://localhost:8000 ``` Store a memory with `POST /api/memories`, search with `POST /api/search`, retrieve by tag with `POST /api/search/by-tag`. Send `X-Agent-ID: ` on a store request and the server tags the memory `agent:`, which a tag search then scopes retrieval by. Worked examples per framework, the tag conventions and the async patterns: **[docs/agents/](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/tree/main/docs/agents)**
OpenCode ```bash MCP_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_ACCESS=true memory server --http ``` The plugin ships as repository files for the local plugin directory, so clone the repository once even if you installed from PyPI. Install steps, the `/memory` slash command and the endpoint override: **[opencode/README.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/opencode/README.md)**
claude.ai and ChatGPT (browser — Remote MCP) Remote MCP puts persistent memory in the browser on any device, no desktop app required: OAuth 2.0 over HTTPS, self-hosted or cloud-hosted. Both claude.ai and ChatGPT (Developer Mode) connect to the same endpoint. Cloudflare Tunnel quick start, Let's Encrypt, nginx, Caddy and Docker production setups: **[Remote MCP Setup](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/remote-mcp-setup.md)** · [5-minute tutorial](https://mcpmemory.services/blog/remote-mcp-tutorial.html)
Advanced: custom backends and team setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service.git cd mcp-memory-service python scripts/installation/install.py ``` Choose from **SQLite** (local, fast, single-user), **Cloudflare** (cloud, multi-device sync), **Hybrid** (5ms local reads with background cloud sync — recommended for production) or **Milvus** (dedicated vector DB: Lite file, self-hosted, or Zilliz Cloud). For long-lived services, prefer Docker Milvus or Zilliz Cloud over Milvus Lite — [why](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/milvus-backend.md#which-uri-to-use).
--- ## ⚡ Works With Your Favorite AI Tools - **Agent frameworks (REST):** LangGraph · CrewAI · AutoGen · OpenClaw/Nanobot · any HTTP client - **CLI and terminal (MCP):** Claude Code · Gemini CLI · OpenCode · Codex CLI · Goose · Aider · Amp - **Desktop and IDE (MCP):** Claude Desktop · VS Code · Cursor · Windsurf · Raycast · JetBrains · Zed - **Chat (MCP):** ChatGPT (Developer Mode) · claude.ai (Remote MCP over HTTPS) Full list, plus clients without OAuth such as Home Assistant: **[docs/integrations.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/integrations.md)** --- ## ✨ Features 🧠 **Persistent Memory** – Context survives across sessions with semantic search 🔍 **Smart Retrieval** – Finds relevant context automatically using AI embeddings ⚡ **5ms Speed** – Instant context injection, no latency ☁️ **Cloud Sync** – Optional Cloudflare backend for team collaboration 🔒 **Privacy-First** – Local-first, you control your data 📊 **Web Dashboard** – Visualize and manage memories at `http://localhost:8000` 🧬 **Knowledge Graph** – Interactive D3.js visualization of memory relationships 🏠 **Homelab Quality Scoring** – Point scoring at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LiteLLM, vLLM) 🔗 **Entity Extraction** – Auto-links @mentions, #tags, URLs, and file paths to a queryable entity graph 💡 **Insight Cards** – Consolidation surfaces patterns, trends, and knowledge gaps as structured insights 🏷️ **Tag Match Filtering** – `tag_match=AND/OR` on `memory_search` for precise multi-tag queries The dashboard has eight tabs — Dashboard, Search, Browse, Documents, Manage, Analytics, Quality, API Docs. [Two-minute walkthrough on YouTube](https://youtu.be/W34r8VFoSdQ) · [Web Dashboard Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/wiki/Web-Dashboard-Guide) How it compares to Mem0, Zep and the MCP-native alternatives, benchmark results, and deployments people run in production: **[mcpmemory.services](https://mcpmemory.services)** --- ## 🛠️ Configuration Highlights ```bash memory launch # Start HTTP server in background (127.0.0.1:8000) memory launch --port 8192 # Custom port memory info # Status and health memory logs --lines 50 # Recent logs memory stop # Stop server ``` These commands are optimized for fast startup and avoid loading heavy ML dependencies unless needed. > ⚠️ **Security note:** the server binds to `127.0.0.1` (localhost only) by default. > `--host 0.0.0.0` / `MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` exposes the API to your network — do that > only in trusted environments with authentication and firewall rules, or behind TLS > termination or a VPN overlay. Backends, embedding models, quality scoring and every environment variable: **[Configuration Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/mastery/configuration-guide.md)** --- ## 📚 Documentation - **[Setup Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/setup-guide.md)** – Decision tree and step-by-step paths - **[Agent Integration Guides](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/tree/main/docs/agents)** – LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, HTTP generic - **[Remote MCP Setup](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/remote-mcp-setup.md)** – claude.ai and ChatGPT via HTTPS + OAuth - **[Configuration Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/mastery/configuration-guide.md)** – Backend options and customization - **[Architecture Overview](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/architecture.md)** – How it works under the hood - **[Knowledge Graph Dashboard](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/features/knowledge-graph-dashboard.md)** – Interactive graph visualization - **[Benchmarks](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md)** – LongMemEval, DevBench, LoCoMo, with run commands - **[Migration Guide](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md)** – Upgrading between major versions - **[Troubleshooting](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/tree/main/docs/troubleshooting)** – Common issues and solutions - **[Wiki](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/wiki)** – Long-form guides and API reference - **[Full documentation index](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/README.md)** – Everything else Also listed on [Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service) and [Spark](https://spark.entire.vc/mcps/vb-mcp-memory-service). --- ## 📦 Releases Every release, with upgrade notes: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/releases) · [archived history](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/docs/archive/CHANGELOG-HISTORIC.md) --- ## 🤝 Contributing We welcome contributions! See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines and [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for reporting a vulnerability. Who authors this project, who holds copyright, and what every change passes before it reaches `main`: [AUTHORSHIP.md](https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/AUTHORSHIP.md). **Quick Development Setup:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service.git cd mcp-memory-service pip install -e . # Editable install pytest tests/ # Run test suite ```
